tasks.short: Enter and check shipment records, resolving missing or inconsistent logistics data.

steps.what: Retrieve shipment events from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and the {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Match shipment references, locations, dates and units against existing records.
Rekey validated shipment details into the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Check saved records for duplicates, omissions and incorrect totals.
Obtain missing evidence and correct disputed shipment details.
Notify dispatchers that records are ready or exceptions remain.

tasks.design: Configure structured feeds into the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with a deterministic adapter where native mappings are insufficient. Validate references, prevent duplicate writes and reconcile totals before publishing status through the {WORKFLOW}; an exception form captures evidence and approved corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Partner formats, inconsistent references and limited integration capacity made rekeying easier to start than maintaining a reliable feed.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing import functions and faster integration development make validation, retries and reconciliation cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Missing source events, conflicting shipment references and partner changes still require investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Establish which source reflects the physical shipment when records disagree.

ambition.what: A shipment-data readiness queue for dispatchers

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time resolving disputed records and preventing recurring data defects. No additional shipment-release or financial authority is assumed.

reach.task: Capture receipt and dispatch events accurately
reach.learn: Scanner event meanings, correction permissions and physical evidence requirements

evidence.claim: Structured imports, reference validation and duplicate prevention can replace routine logistics rekeying.
Source completeness and conflicting identifiers remain common integration exceptions.

assumptions: The representative flow uses structured shipment events; document-only sources would require additional work.
The integration posts validated records in s2, removing separate rekeying in s3.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges cover one shipment feed and one destination. Consultation under national rules is included where employee monitoring changes.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability must be assessed for the implemented use; this design does not score workers.
unknowns: Supported interfaces, import licences and write permissions
Actual shipment identifiers, exception volumes and correction authority
Whether personal data or employee monitoring triggers additional consultation
research_questions: Which supported import mechanism preserves validation, event ordering and recovery after partial failure?
new_work: Resolve rejected records and conflicting evidence.
Maintain field mappings and reference data.
Check reconciliation failures and partner format changes.

tasks.short: Track logistics costs, procurement delays, back orders and delivery performance, then explain exceptions.

steps.what: Retrieve freight costs and purchasing commitments from the {ERP}.
Retrieve shipment, inventory and back-order status from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Join extracts and reconcile rates, quantities, currencies and reporting periods in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Compare cost, backlog and delivery measures against targets in the {BI}.
Discuss major exceptions with dispatchers, purchasing staff and warehouse supervisors.
Prepare the logistics briefing with verified explanations and proposed actions.
Circulate the approved briefing and assign follow-up requests.

tasks.design: Schedule validated extracts from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, then configure exception views in the {BI}. Generate a briefing from fixed metric templates and structured analyst explanations, with analyst approval before the {WORKFLOW} distributes it and creates follow-up requests in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reporting definitions, shipment-to-charge joins and reporting periods differed across systems and teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled extracts and reusable metric definitions are established techniques; faster coding reduces the cost of reconciliation and report generation.
tasks.still_hard: Accrual timing, incomplete carrier events and causal explanations can make apparently clear trends misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Separate genuine service problems from timing effects and agree useful investigations with operational teams.
tasks.altitude: The analyst reviews exceptions daily and spends less time assembling recurring reports. They can select investigations within an agreed remit; spending decisions retain their existing approval route.

reach.task: Prioritise follow-up on delayed parts and back orders
reach.learn: Allocation rules, production dependencies and promised-date changes
Service commitments, cost ownership and escalation thresholds

evidence.claim: Checking freight charges against contracted rates is an existing software capability.
Recurring logistics measures and fixed reporting templates can run deterministically.

assumptions: Recurring measures have agreed definitions; new analytical questions belong to a separate modelling task.
The briefing uses fixed text templates and analyst-entered explanations, so a language model is unnecessary.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
Build ranges cover one reporting scope and two source systems. Access and applicable consultation under national rules are included.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability must be assessed if reporting expands into identifiable worker evaluation.
unknowns: Metric definitions, data latency and existing reporting capabilities
Whether costs include accruals, surcharges and currency adjustments
Who may assign investigations and approve operational changes
research_questions: Which native reporting and scheduling functions can satisfy the agreed metric definitions without custom code?
new_work: Investigate reconciliation failures and material exceptions.
Maintain metric definitions, thresholds and recipient permissions.
Review briefing explanations and follow-up completion.

tasks.short: Model logistics alternatives and assess their costs, benefits and operational consequences.

steps.what: Agree the decision question, alternatives and constraints with the supply chain manager.
Retrieve relevant shipment, cost, inventory and service records.
Clean and join records, documenting exclusions and data gaps in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Specify cost drivers, operational constraints, assumptions and comparison methods.
Calculate baseline costs and alternative scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Challenge results against historical outcomes and sensitivity tests.
Write the business case, including trade-offs, uncertainty and a recommended pilot.

loop.input: Validated scenario results, model limitations and the analyst's model specification
loop.output: A draft business case with source references and explicit uncertainties
loop.check: Check every number against scenario outputs; the analyst checks reasoning, omissions and the recommendation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved checks fall back to a fixed template and manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but varied decision questions require contextual prose beyond a fixed reporting template.

steps.what: Decide whether to approve the proposed pilot and its limits.

tasks.design: Build reusable data preparation and scenario calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with assumptions and sensitivity controls exposed through the {BI}. A bounded drafting loop prepares a business case in the {DOCS} from validated outputs; the analyst approves the document and the supply chain manager separately authorises a pilot in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each study rebuilt data joins and calculations, while operational assumptions remained buried in individual workbooks.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster coding makes reusable calculation modules and validation checks more affordable. Bounded drafting can summarise checked results without controlling the model or committing resources.
tasks.still_hard: Sparse observations, changing demand, hidden capacity constraints and uncertain causal effects limit model reliability.
tasks.human_edge: Choose defensible assumptions and recognise when an attractive numerical result would fail operationally.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more of the week challenging assumptions and designing measurable pilots. They gain capacity to shape pilot options; approval of spending and service changes remains with the authorised manager.

reach.task: Select transport and inventory improvement pilots
reach.learn: Risk appetite, service trade-offs and investment criteria

reach.task: Define pilot measures and implementation milestones
reach.learn: Baseline design, dependencies and benefit verification

evidence.claim: Operational route planning is an established software capability; this supports technical feasibility, not a customer-specific benefit estimate.
Scenario calculations, sensitivity tests and data validation can use deterministic methods.
A documented report failure involving invented citations supports checking generated business-case claims against supplied evidence.

assumptions: The first build covers one decision family, such as shipment consolidation, rather than arbitrary logistics questions.
Only source preparation, calculations and drafting are automated; model framing and pilot authorisation remain human.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates; novel models may save less time.
Build ranges include back-testing and a limited pilot. Access and applicable employee consultation under national rules are included.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability require assessment if models affect identifiable workers or their evaluation.
unknowns: First decision family, usable historical outcomes and available cost drivers
Existing calculation tools and analyst modelling skills
Pilot approval limits and whether proposed changes affect employee working arrangements
research_questions: Which deterministic model is adequate for the chosen decision and available data?
Which historical comparisons can reveal unstable assumptions before a pilot?
new_work: Maintain model specifications and calculation versions.
Review generated business cases against source outputs.
Back-test assumptions and measure pilot outcomes.

tasks.short: Monitor warehouse inventory transactions and investigate discrepancies in receiving, storage and shipping.

steps.what: Review receiving, movement and shipping transactions in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Compare transaction totals with receipt, dispatch and stock records.
List missing movements, quantity differences and unusual adjustments in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Trace flagged transactions and assess whether physical checks are needed.
Check affected locations and count stock where records remain uncertain.
Determine likely causes and recommend corrections or further investigation.
Approve, reject or return proposed stock corrections for further evidence.

tasks.design: Configure inventory exception views in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, adding deterministic reconciliation on the {DATA_PLATFORM} where cross-record checks are missing. A case record in the {WORKFLOW} links transaction evidence, count findings and decisions; stock corrections require warehouse supervisor approval before execution in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Transaction histories, physical evidence and adjustment approvals were reviewed separately, making discrepancies slow to trace.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exception reports and cheaper reconciliation code can assemble evidence without requiring a model to judge stock movements.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded physical movements, delayed postings, damaged goods and ambiguous count evidence remain operational problems.
tasks.human_edge: Test the record against the warehouse floor and distinguish a posting issue from a real stock loss.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time scanning normal transactions and more time selecting discrepancies for investigation. Count priorities can be proposed daily; stock-adjustment authority follows the existing approval limits.

reach.task: Investigate location discrepancies and perform cycle counts
reach.learn: Physical handling sequences, count controls and unit conversions
Root-cause methods, evidence standards and corrective-action verification

evidence.claim: Inventory reconciliation, sequence checks and exception dashboards can use deterministic controls.
Physical counts and investigation remain necessary when recorded movements do not establish actual stock.

assumptions: The representative scope is inventory integrity; warehouse activity monitoring does not automatically imply worker evaluation.
Physical checks occur only for selected exceptions; shares average their contribution across the monitoring workflow.
Reconciliation assumes accessible structured receipt and dispatch records. Paper-only evidence would increase effort.
Time shares include warehouse and approval handoffs and are planning estimates.
Build ranges cover one warehouse. Access and consultation under national rules are included where monitoring changes.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability must be assessed before adding identifiable worker scoring.
unknowns: Transaction completeness, posting delays and available location histories
Existing exception reports and inventory adjustment controls
Count capacity, approval thresholds and employee consultation requirements
research_questions: Which native controls expose transaction lineage and prevent duplicate or unauthorised adjustments?
Which reconciliation tolerances distinguish normal posting delays from actionable discrepancies?
new_work: Tune exception thresholds and investigate false alerts.
Maintain receipt, movement and dispatch mappings.
Review unresolved cases and repeated control failures.
Check that approved corrections retain their supporting evidence.

role.altitude: The logistics analyst shifts from assembling records and recurring reports toward investigating exceptions, testing assumptions and designing operational pilots. Broader spending, stock-adjustment or service-change rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Shipping, receiving, and inventory clerks: connect transaction evidence with physical handling and counts.
Production, planning, and expediting clerks: connect backlog analysis with allocation and production dependencies.
Supply chain managers: translate analytical findings into bounded operational pilots.
Project management specialists: define pilot baselines and verify realised benefits.
skills_to_grow: Data reconciliation and logistics event semantics
Root-cause investigation and physical evidence assessment
Review of generated prose against source calculations
role.ambitious_version: Run a logistics improvement service that identifies emerging cost and service problems, prepares tested options and measures pilot outcomes across transport, procurement and warehouse operations.
